keyVerseText: Behold, I will send for many fishers , saith the LORD, and they shall fish them; and after will I send for many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain, and from every hill, and out of the holes of the rocks.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun צַיָּד (tsayâd) derives from the root צַיִד (tsayid), which encompasses notions of hunting, capturing food, and provision. This root highlights not only the act of pursuing game but also the outcome—food or sustenance obtained through the chase. Thus, the literal sense of tsayâd extends beyond the simple English term 'hunter' to imply one who actively secures provision by skillful pursuit, emphasizing both effort and reward in the context of survival and sustenance.
usageInScripture: The term צַיָּד appears only once in the Hebrew Bible, specifically in Jeremiah 16:16, where it is translated as 'hunters' in the plural form צַיָּדִים. This consistent translation underscores the word's clear association with those who hunt, reinforcing its concrete meaning without ambiguity. The limited occurrence suggests a specialized use, highlighting the role of hunters as agents who pursue and capture, which in this context is applied metaphorically to God's intervention.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding צַיָּד as a hunter who actively seeks and secures provision enriches our grasp of God's sovereign activity in Scripture. The imagery of hunters portrays God as one who not only calls but pursues His people with purpose and determination, ensuring His plans are fulfilled. This reflects the divine initiative in salvation, where God is the pursuer who brings the scattered back to Himself. Recognizing this word's meaning invites believers to trust in God's proactive care and the certainty of His gathering work, which ultimately points to Christ as the fulfillment of God's redemptive chase.
keyVerseReflection: Jeremiah 16:16 declares, 'Behold, I will send for many fishers, saith the LORD, and they shall fish them; and after will I send for many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain, and from every hill, and out of the holes of the rocks.' The term 'hunters' here conveys God's determined pursuit of His people, complementing the earlier image of fishers. It emphasizes the thoroughness and inevitability of God's gathering, reaching even the most hidden places. The word צַיָּד thus deepens the verse's portrayal of God's active and relentless care in bringing His scattered people back into His fold.
